questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the percentage error in the physical quantity $A$ If it is related to four other physical quantities $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ as $A = \dfrac{{a}^{2}{b}^{3}}{d\sqrt{c}}$? The percentage error in measurement of $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are$1 %$, $3 %$, $2 %$ and $1 %$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Percentage error in $A$

$= 2\dfrac{\Deltaa}{a} + 3\dfrac{\Deltab}{b} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\Deltac}{c} + \dfrac{\Deltad}{d}$

$= \left(2 \times 1 + 3 \times 3 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 + 1 \times 1\right) % = 13 %$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student measures the distance covered and time taken by a body under free fall which was initially at rest. He uses this data for estimating $g$, the acceleration due to gravity. If the maximum percentage errors in measurement of the distance and the time are ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2}$ respectively, then the maximum possible percentage error in the estimation of $g$& is
questions.solution:
From the relation

$\text{h} = \text{ut} + \dfrac{1}{2} {\text{gt}}^{2}$

$\text{h} = \dfrac{1}{2} {\text{gt}}^{2} ⇒ \text{g} = \dfrac{2 \text{h}}{{\text{t}}^{2}} \left(∵ \text{body initially at rest}\right)$

Taking natural logarithms on both sides, we get

$ln\left(g\right) = ln\left(h\right) - 2ln\left(t\right) + ln\left(2\right)$

$\text{Differentiating,} \dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{\text{g}} = \dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{\text{h}} - 2 \dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{\text{t}}$

For maximum permissible errors, we add both the errors. So

${\left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{\text{g}} \times 100\right)}_{\text{max}} = \left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{\text{h}} \times \text{100}\right) + 2 \times \left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{\text{t}} \times \text{100}\right)$


$\dfrac{\Delta \text{h}}{\text{h}} \times \text{100} = {\text{e}}_{1} \text{and} \dfrac{\Delta \text{t}}{\text{t}} \times \text{100} = {\text{e}}_{2}$

$\text{Therefore,} {\left(\dfrac{\Delta \text{g}}{\text{g}} \times \text{100}\right)}_{\text{max}} = {\text{e}}_{1} + 2 {\text{e}}_{2}$

questions.q: A glass hemisphere $\left(\mu = \text{1.5}\right)$ has a radius of curvature of $16$ cm. A small object $O$ is located on its axis halfway between the plane and spherical surface. The distance between two images, when viewed along the axis from the sides of the hemisphere, is
questions.solution:
When viewed from spherical side,
$\dfrac{1}{v1} + \dfrac{3}{2 \times 8} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times 16}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v1} = \dfrac{1}{32} - \dfrac{3}{16} = \dfrac{- 5}{32}$
Image position is $\dfrac{32}{5}cm$ inside the hemisphere from its periphery.
And when viewed from plane side then image is at $\dfrac{16}{3}cm$ inside the plane surface.
$∴ \Delta x = 16 - \dfrac{16}{3} - \dfrac{32}{5} = \dfrac{64}{15}cm$

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $25Ω$ is connected to a battery of $2V$ along with a resistance of $3000Ω$. In this case, a full-scale deflection of $30units$ is obtained in the galvanometer. In order to reduce this deflection to $10units$, how much more resistance (in $Ω$) should be added to the circuit in series?
questions.solution:
The deflection in a galvanometer is directly proportional to the current.

First case:

$30x = \dfrac{2}{25 + 3000}$

Second case:

$10x = \dfrac{2}{25 + 3000 + R}$

$⇒ 3 = \dfrac{25 + 3000 + R}{25 + 3000}$

On solving, we get

$R = 6050Ω$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The length of a magnet is large compared to its width and breadth. The time period of its oscillation in a vibration magnetometer is $2s$. The magnent is cut into three equal parts of length $\dfrac{L}{3}$ each,and three parts are then placed on each other with their like poles together. The time period of this combination will be
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillations of magnet

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{I}{M{B}_{H}}\right)} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Where $I =$ moment of inertia of magnet

$= \dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{12}$ (m, being the mass of magnet)

Now magnet is cut into three equal parts.

When the three equal parts of magnet are placed on one another with their like poles together, then

${I}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{m}{3}\right) \times {\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)}^{2} \times 3$

$= \dfrac{1}{12}\dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{I}{9}$

and ${M}^{′} =$ pole strength $\times \dfrac{L}{3} \times 3 = M$

Hence,

$⇒ {T}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times T$

${T}^{′} = \dfrac{2}{3}s$

questions.q: A standard cell of $1.08V$ is balanced by the potential difference across $90cm$ of a $1$ meter, long wire supplied by a cell of emf $2V$ through a series resistor of resistance $2Ω$. If the internal resistance of cell in the primary circuit is zero then the resistance per unit length (in $Ω{m}^{- 1}$) of potentiometer wire is
questions.solution:
$E = X . l( X = \text{Potential}\text{gradient} )$

$E = \left(\dfrac{{E}_{o}}{L} \times \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + r + {R}_{h}}\right) \times l\left(∵ r = 0, {R}_{h} = 2Ω\right)$

$∴ 1.08 = \left(\dfrac{2}{1m} \times \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}\right) \times 0.90m$

$\dfrac{1.08}{2 \times 0.90} = \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}$

Hence : $0.6 = \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}$

$0.6{R}_{w} + 1.2 = {R}_{w} ⇒ 1.2 = 0.4{R}_{w} ⇒ 3 = {R}_{w}$

$∴$ Resistance per unit length is $3Ω{m}^{- 1}$

Current in tangent galvanometer

$I = \dfrac{2r{B}_{H}}{{\mu}_{0}N}tan ⁡ \theta . . \left(i\right)$

$\dfrac{rtan ⁡ \theta}{N} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2{B}_{H}} = \text{same for both}$

$⇒ \dfrac{8 \times 1}{\left(2\right)\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{{N}_{B}}$

$∴ {N}_{B} = 12turns$

When the three equal parts of magnet are placed on one another with their like poles together, then

${I}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{m}{3}\right) \times {\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)}^{2} \times 3$

$= \dfrac{1}{12}\dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{I}{9}$

and ${M}^{′} =$ pole strength $\times \dfrac{L}{3} \times 3 = M$

Hence,

$⇒ {T}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times T$

$⇒ {T}^{′} = \dfrac{150}{3} = 50ms$

questions.q: A professor reads a greeting card received on his 50th birthday with + 2.5 D glasses keeping the card 25 cm away. Ten years letter, he reads his farewell letter with the same glasses but he has to keep the letter 50 cm away. What should be the power (in dioptre) of the lens now so that he can keep the letter at the same distance as ten years ago?
questions.solution:
Firstly find out distance of retina from his eye lens i.e., image distance in first case (we are assuming distance between eye lens and retina is not changing which is not true practically we are taking that liberty to make problem more mathematically convenient. However it doesn't effect base line of problem)

$\dfrac{1}{\text{v}} - \dfrac{1}{- 2 5} = \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{1}}$

$\dfrac{1}{\text{v}} + \dfrac{1}{2 5} = \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{1}}$

for second case image distance should be same

$\dfrac{1}{\text{v}} + \dfrac{1}{5 0} = \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2 5} - \dfrac{1}{5 0} = \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 {cm}^{- 1}}{5 0} = \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{f ⁡}_{2}} = {\text{P}}_{1} - {\text{P}}_{2} = 2 \text{D}$

Let power of his eye lens in two cases are (Pe)1, (Pe)2 respectively

${\text{P}}_{1} = \left(\text{2.5} + {\left({\text{P}}_{\text{e}}\right)}_{1}\right)$

${\text{P}}_{2} = \left(\text{2.5} + {\left({\text{P}}_{\text{e}}\right)}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ {\text{P}}_{1} - {\text{P}}_{2} = {\left({\text{P}}_{\text{e}}\right)}_{1} - {\left({\text{P}}_{\text{e}}\right)}_{2}$

= 2 D

So loss in power is 2 D so he should use additional power of 2 D i.e. 4.5 D

questions.q: A standard cell of $1.08V$ is balanced by the potential difference across $90cm$ of a $1$ meter, long wire supplied by a cell of emf $2V$ through a series resistor of resistance $2Ω$. If the internal resistance of cell in the primary circuit is zero then the resistance per unit length (in $Ω{m}^{- 1}$) of potentiometer wire is
questions.solution:
$E = X . l( X = \text{Potential}\text{gradient} )$

$E = \left(\dfrac{{E}_{o}}{L} \times \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + r + {R}_{h}}\right) \times l\left(∵ r = 0, {R}_{h} = 2Ω\right)$

$∴ 1.08 = \left(\dfrac{2}{1m} \times \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}\right) \times 0.90m$

$\dfrac{1.08}{2 \times 0.90} = \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}$

Hence : $0.6 = \dfrac{{R}_{w}}{{R}_{w} + 2}$

$0.6{R}_{w} + 1.2 = {R}_{w} ⇒ 1.2 = 0.4{R}_{w} ⇒ 3 = {R}_{w}$

$∴$ Resistance per unit length is $3Ω{m}^{- 1}$

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, resistances are connected as shown in figure. The balancing length ${l}_{1} = 55 cm$ . Now, an unknown resistance $x$ is connected in series with $P$ and the new balancing length is found to be $75cm$ . What is the value of The value of $11x$ (in ohm)?(Given, $P = 4Ω$ )
questions.solution:
Given in the meter bridge,

In $I$ st case, $\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{Q} = \dfrac{55}{100 - 55}$

$⇒ Q = \dfrac{4 \times 45}{55}$ ...(i)

In $2$ nd case, $\dfrac{P + x}{Q} = \dfrac{75}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4 + x}{3} = Q$ ...(ii)

From Equations (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{4 + x}{3} = \dfrac{36}{11}$

$4 + x = \dfrac{108}{11}$

$x = \dfrac{108 - 44}{11}$

$= \dfrac{64}{11}$

$⇒ 11x = 64$
